parsed.hook: Comando G's El Reventón sits on granite outcrops at 900 meters in Cebreros, where Garnacha vines have deep roots. The 2020 vintage clocks in at 15% ABV with 14 months in oak, a deliberate choice to tame the heat of the high-altitude site.
parsed.wine_summary:
Comando G is a small project from Fernando García and Daniel Landi that has shifted the conversation around Sierra de Gredos Garnacha. They farm old vines on granite and focus on site expression over power. El Reventón is their top bottling, from vines planted on granite and schist at high elevation, where cooler nights preserve acidity.

The appellation rules state that Cebreros reds are Garnacha-dominant, with old vines on granite and Albillo Real white grape allowed up to 40% in blends. Comando G keeps the focus on Garnacha, but the white grape can be used for freshness. Alicante Bouschet adds color depth and tannic structure. The result is a wine that reads as dark and savory, with granite-driven minerality.
parsed.terroir_expression: The Sierra de Gredos is a granite batholith, and Cebreros sits on the southern flank where granite and schist meet. El Reventón's vines grow in decomposed granite soils at 900 meters, with a continental climate marked by hot days and sharp diurnal swings. That elevation slows ripening, keeping acidity fresh even in warm vintages. The granite soils drain well and impart a stony, savory edge to the wine, while the schist adds tannic grip. Alicante Bouschet's pigmented flesh gives the wine its ink-dark color and structural heft, but the old-vine Garnacha provides the core of red fruit and herbal lift.
parsed.vinification_summary: Comando G uses native yeasts and a mix of concrete and large oak for fermentation, then ages the wine for 14 months in neutral vessels. The 2020 vintage saw 14 months in oak, a choice to soften tannins without adding new oak flavor. The winery practices biodynamic farming, which means they use compost teas and avoid synthetic inputs to build soil life. The result is a wine that feels focused rather than overworked.
food_pairing: Paella Valenciana — the wine's granite-driven minerality and savory edge cut through the rice's richness, while its dark fruit complements the rabbit and snails.
Nashville hot chicken — the wine's tannic structure and herbal lift stand up to the heat and spice, while the dark fruit balances the fried chicken fat.
Grilled lamb chops with rosemary — the wine's old-vine Garnacha character and earthy depth mirror the lamb's gaminess, while the tannins clean the palate.
Aged Manchego and quince paste — the wine's savory notes and firm tannins contrast the cheese's fat and the paste's sweetness.
Mushroom risotto with Parmesan — the wine's earthy, stony profile matches the mushrooms, while the tannins handle the creamy texture.
similar_wines: Terroir al Límit 'Les Manyes' — both are single-vineyard Garnacha from high-elevation granite sites, with a focus on minerality and structure.
Cims de Porrera 'Vinyes Velles' — old-vine Garnacha from Priorat's slate soils, sharing the dark fruit and tannic heft but with a different mineral profile.
parsed.style_profile: Full-bodied dry red with firm tannins and granite-driven minerality
parsed.cellar_recommendation: Drink from 2025 to 2030. Store in a cool, dark place with stable temperature and humidity.
parsed.value_assessment: At $70–$90, El Reventón sits in the same price range as Terroir al Límit 'Les Manyes' and Cims de Porrera 'Vinyes Velles'. It's worth it for the unique high-altitude granite expression and the winery's consistent quality.
parsed.market_position: This wine appears on fine-dining wine lists in Madrid and Barcelona, and on specialty retail shelves in the US and UK. Collectors seek out Comando G's single-vineyard bottlings, while curious Garnacha drinkers pick it up to explore Sierra de Gredos.
parsed.insider_take: If you expect a fruit-forward Garnacha, this will surprise you — it's savory, stony, and structured. Skip it if you prefer soft, easy-drinking reds; buy it if you want a wine that reflects its granite terroir.
